$comment: Where every vendored file came from. Data, not code, so that re-fetching is a
mechanical operation and reviewing an upgrade is reading one diff.
The authoritative copy of each hash is the `integrity` block in index.html,
because that is the one the browser enforces. The hashes here must agree with
it, and `npm run verify` fails if they drift. `npm run vendor` re-downloads
each url and refuses to overwrite a local file unless the freshly downloaded
bytes match the hash already recorded, so a compromised or silently rebuilt
upstream cannot land in this repository without an explicit --accept-new and
a visible diff.
Every url is a static published file pinned to an exact version. jsDelivr's
generated artefacts are avoided on purpose: /+esm bundles and the implicit
.min.js it synthesises are built on demand, and jsDelivr's own output warns
against SRI-pinning them. @tailwindcss/browser is therefore pinned to
dist/index.global.js, the real published file, and not to the bare package
URL that resolves to a generated dist/index.global.min.js.
`license` is the SPDX identifier the upstream package declares, and
`licenseCovers` names every package whose code the vendored file contains —
one for a single-package file, four for the Lit bundle. Both MIT and
BSD-3-Clause require the notice to travel with the copy, and these files are
committed, so the copy is this repository. LICENSES.md holds the texts.
`npm run vendor` checks that every entry here has a section there and that
its text still matches the LICENSE in node_modules for the same pinned
version, which is the same shape as the hash check: a notice somebody can
edit without touching the bytes it covers is not a control.

files.note: The all-in-one bundle, so the shell and every remote share one Lit instance and `repeat` is included.
Imported only by source/lib/core/foundation/reactive.js, which is the seam for replacing it.
Browser JIT for development. Contains no fetch, XHR or WebAssembly, so it needs no network of its own. Production links the compiled app.css instead and never loads this.
